text_blocks.snippet: An infected hemangioma, a common complication, occurs when a benign tumor of extra blood vessels (hemangioma) becomes infected, typically by bacteria. Signs of infection include pain, redness, pus, skin breakdown (ulceration), and sometimes fever. Treatment often involves antibiotics, and in some cases, other medications like beta-blockers or corticosteroids may be used to manage the hemangioma itself.
